response.answer:
For a renter with a balcony, I'd recommend a portable solar panel + battery power station setup. It's renter-friendly, requires no permanent installation, and can move with you when your lease ends.

The main decision is whether you want to power a few devices using sunlight or reduce your apartment's electricity bill. Those require different systems.

Best setup for a renter

A typical setup consists of:

Solar panel: 100–400W, ideally mounted or placed where it gets direct sunlight.

Battery: 500–2,000Wh LiFePO4 portable power station.

Inverter: Built into the power station, providing normal AC outlets.

No electrical modifications: Plug devices directly into the power station.

You can use it to run a laptop, router, lights, fans, and some small appliances. A larger battery may also power a refrigerator for a limited period.

For a renter with a balcony, I'd recommend a **portable solar panel + battery power station** setup. It's renter-friendly, requires no permanent installation, and can move with you when your lease ends.

The main decision is whether you want to **power a few devices using sunlight** or **reduce your apartment's electricity bill**. Those require different systems.

## Best setup for a renter

<AsyncImageGroup query={["portable folding solar panel on apartment balcony connected to portable power station","EcoFlow portable power station solar panel balcony setup","Anker SOLIX portable power station solar panel outdoor balcony"]} aspectRatio="5:4" layout="carousel" shop_eligible={true}/>

A typical setup consists of:

- **Solar panel:** 100–400W, ideally mounted or placed where it gets direct sunlight.
- **Battery:** 500–2,000Wh LiFePO4 portable power station.
- **Inverter:** Built into the power station, providing normal AC outlets.
- **No electrical modifications:** Plug devices directly into the power station.

You can use it to run a laptop, router, lights, fans, and some small appliances. A larger battery may also power a refrigerator for a limited period.

## Solar + battery systems worth considering

      **<Entity ref="turn845085product8" value={turn845085product8.title}/>**

      <text color="secondary" size="xs">1,024Wh battery + 100W panel</text>
      <title size="lg" color="default" tabularNums>{turn845085product8.displayed_price}</title>
      Good starter setup for a smaller balcony and basic backup power.
      <text size="xs"><Link url={turn845085product8.product_page.uri} title="View at B&H"/></text>
    </box>

    <box flex="1" gap={1}>

      <text color="secondary" size="xs">1,024Wh battery + 200W panel</text>

      <title size="lg" color="default" tabularNums>{turn845085product22.displayed_price}</title>
      Alternative portable kit with a LiFePO4 battery and 1,500W AC output.
      <text size="xs"><Link url={turn845085product22.product_page.uri} title="View product"/></text>
    </box>

</box>

## How much electricity could you generate?

Here's an illustrative estimate for a balcony receiving about 3 hours of equivalent full sunlight daily, after allowing for system losses.

{@body const [watts,setWatts] = DIL.useState(200)}
{@body const [sun,setSun] = DIL.useState(3)}
{@body const daily = watts*sun*0.75/1000}
<box border radius="xl" padding={3} gap={3}>
  <row align="center" justify="between">
    **Panel capacity**
    <title size="lg" color="default" tabularNums>{watts} W</title>
  </row>
  <slider min={100} max={400} step={50} value={watts} onChange={setWatts}/>
  <row align="center" justify="between">
    **Daily equivalent full-sun hours**
    <title size="lg" color="default" tabularNums>{sun} h</title>
  </row>
  <slider min={1} max={6} step={0.5} value={sun} onChange={setSun}/>
  <divider color="subtle"/>
  <grid columns={2} gap={2}>
    <grid-item>
      <box background="surface-secondary" radius="lg" padding={3} gap={1}>
        <text color="secondary" size="xs">Daily generation</text>
        <title size="xl" color="default" tabularNums>{daily.toFixed(2)} kWh</title>
      </box>
    </grid-item>
    <grid-item>
      <box background="surface-secondary" radius="lg" padding={3} gap={1}>
        <text color="secondary" size="xs">Monthly generation</text>
        <title size="xl" color="default" tabularNums>{(daily*30).toFixed(1)} kWh</title>
      </box>
    </grid-item>
  </grid>
  <caption>Illustrative estimate with a 75% overall energy yield. Actual results depend on balcony direction, shadows, panel angle and weather.</caption>
</box>

## Important: California has a new balcony solar law

If you're renting in California, SB 868 is scheduled to take effect **January 1, 2027**. It creates a simplified path for qualifying certified plug-in solar systems up to 1,200W AC, but it doesn't automatically override rental restrictions. <Cite refs={["turn845085search0","turn845085search4"]}/>

That means you have two choices:

| System | Main advantage |
|---|---|
| Portable solar + battery | Backup power, no connection to apartment wiring |
| Certified plug-in balcony solar, potentially with battery | Can offset electricity used throughout your apartment |

Do not plug a conventional portable power station's AC output into a wall outlet. Grid-connected systems need appropriate certification and safeguards.

## Two questions to narrow this down

{@body const [goal,setGoal] = DIL.useState("bill")}
{@body const [direction,setDirection] = DIL.useState("south")}
<box border radius="xl" padding={3} gap={3}>
  <form gap={3} onSubmit={()=>GenUI.issueNewTurn("Recommend a renter-friendly balcony solar panel and battery setup. My primary goal is "+(goal==="bill"?"reducing my electricity bill":goal==="backup"?"backup power during outages":"both savings and backup")+". My balcony faces "+direction+". Include suitable products, sizing and cost estimates.")}>
    <box gap={2}>
      <label>What's your main goal?</label>
      <radio-group direction="col" value={goal} onChange={setGoal}>
        <radio value="bill">Lower my electricity bill</radio>
        <radio value="backup">Backup power during outages</radio>
        <radio value="both">Both</radio>
      </radio-group>
    </box>
    <divider color="subtle"/>
    <box gap={2}>
      <label>Which direction does your balcony face?</label>
      <radio-group direction="col" value={direction} onChange={setDirection}>
        <radio value="south">South</radio>
        <radio value="east">East</radio>
        <radio value="west">West</radio>
        <radio value="north">North</radio>
        <radio value="unknown">Not sure</radio>
      </radio-group>
    </box>
    <button block submit>Find my best setup <icon name="arrow-right" inline/></button>
  </form>
</box>

## Solar + battery systems worth considering
